question: Should core Skill Workshop approvals become proposal-version-bound so an older prompt cannot approve revised content, while direct service, CLI, and tool lifecycle calls remain proposal-ID-compatible?
rationale: The patch is well-proven, but it adds a new core user-facing capability and intentionally changes stale approval behavior, requiring owner confirmation of the compatibility contract.

options.title: Adopt snapshot-bound approvals
options.body: Keep `proposal_version` optional for direct calls but require the resolved version for approval-derived apply, reject, and quarantine actions.

options.title: Preview without lifecycle binding
options.body: Add read-only review previews but retain ID-only approval execution, accepting that an older prompt could act on revised proposal content.

options.title: Pause the core feature
options.body: Defer or close both linked items until maintainers select a different Skill Workshop review and approval model.

recommendation.title: Adopt snapshot-bound approvals
recommendation.body: Keep `proposal_version` optional for direct calls but require the resolved version for approval-derived apply, reject, and quarantine actions.

likelyOwner.reason: The discussion routed the product review to this candidate, and the decision covers core tool UX and approval policy rather than only implementation details.
